chunks: Saʿd ibn Saʿd asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about the prostration of gratitude, and he said:
I see our companions prostrating once after the obligatory prayer and saying that it is the prostration of gratitude.
So he عليه السلام said: Gratitude is only when Allah bestows a blessing upon His servant, that he says:
Glory be to the One Who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of it, and indeed to our Lord we shall surely return.
And all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

key_terms.أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ: Allah bestowed a blessing or favor
key_terms.الشُّكْرُ: gratitude to Allah for His blessing upon the servant
key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory prayer after which the companions were seen prostrating
key_terms.سَجْدَةِ الشُّكْرِ: the prostration of gratitude performed in thankfulness to Allah
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ: a declaration of Allah's transcendence and glorification
key_terms.مُقْرِنِينَ: fully capable or able to control and master it by ourselves
key_terms.وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ: a declaration that all praise belongs to Allah

ai.seo_question: What should be said in sajdat al-shukr according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses sajdat al-shukr and directs attention to verbal gratitude to Allah when He bestows a blessing. It connects gratitude with praising Allah through exaltation and الحمد, especially using Qur'anic words of recognition and return to Him.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.973 - Sa'd ibn Sa'd asked Imam al-Ridha (as) about the prostration of gratitude (Sajdat al-Shukr).
He said: “I see our companions prostrate once after the obligatory prayer and say that it is the prostration of gratitude.”
Imam (as) replied: “Gratitude is when Allah (swt) bestows a blessing upon His servant, and the servant says,
‘Glory be to the One who has subjected this to us, for we were not capable of it, and indeed to our Lord (azj), we will return. 
And all praise is due to Allah (swt), the Lord (azj) of the worlds.’”
